Yinyang’s philosophy uses characters, imagery, and relationships to organize practice between a person and a model, giving that practice an engineering ontology the model can interpret and use. These documents develop the philosophical work and offer references for psychological-model writing, collaboration, and environment adaptation.

Understand the practice

For readers: understand how the author connects philosophy, collaboration between a person and model, and the working environment.

  • Practice explained

    For readers: explains how the author connects philosophy, understanding the person and counterpart, and the working environment, including methods others can borrow.

Collaboration and methods

Writing references help develop concrete psychological-model files, the collaboration entrypoint reads them, and environment adaptation realizes their understanding in actual work.

  • Yinyang

    Enter collaboration through the available situated accounts and identify understanding still needed; full adoption follows the initial reading contract.

  • Designing and revising a situated Yinyang

    Explains how to form, write, and revise connected accounts through personal material and actual interaction; the five references below address the individual files.

    References for writing the five psychological-model files

    Five writing references built on Yinyang’s philosophical account. Use them with the actual person’s material and interactions to write connected accounts of the encounter, person, counterpart and relationship, situated use, and sources.

    • How to write an encounter account

      Condense purpose, participation, and the relationship into a usable view for ordinary collaboration.

    • How to develop a user model

      Understand the actual person through relevant experience and evidence, retaining scope, differences, and unknowns.

    • How to describe the counterpart and relationship

      Describe the actual counterpart’s capabilities, intended contributions, cooperation, and reciprocal correction.

    • How to describe situated use

      Describe current resources, participant contributions, and conditions; adaptation owns changes to operation and verification of their effects.

    • How to organize sources and grounds

      Locate the grounds of understanding and source owners, retaining authorized routes to original material.

  • Realizing Yinyang in a working harness

    Realize selected understanding through instructions, tools, and the working environment, check actual effects, and revise through feedback.

Views and reading

Consult the author’s claims, arguments, and sources to understand and compare the questions and connections of philosophy, psychology, and engineering.

  • Core views

    Find the author’s main claims and connected arguments, organized by topic.

  • Read by the work being done

    Find relevant arguments, methods, and original sources from the question at hand.

  • Philosophical readings

    Trace thinkers and works to their role in the argument and their original sources.

  • A guide to Lacanian concepts

    An introduction and review tracing the Other, the divided subject, retroaction, the three registers, and the sinthome from original texts into personal philosophy and practice.

  • Psychological readings

    Books and papers on psychological process modeling and evidence, mind and psychological theories, belief, reasoning, and interaction.

  • Engineering readings

    From CS DIY and Missing Semester to Git, Linux, software design, algorithms, experimental implementation, and physical conditions.
